Silencers are regulatory elements that bind to the basal apparatus at the promoter region of the gene, having a positive effect on transcription. The name "silencer" was chosen because they were first discovered while studying genes in which transcription was silent (i.e., not being expressed). The name is misleading as it implies that a silencer will silence a gene by repressing its expression. In truth, the function of a silencer is to enhance the level of transcription from a gene.
